extracted.intended_audience: practicing patent attorneys, equity litigators, and judges handling patent injunctions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing the issuance, dissolution, suspension, reinstatement, scope, duration, and enforcement of preliminary and permanent injunctions in U.S. patent litigation, including appellate review, bonds, persons bound, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolution based on facts arising after injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: A dissolution of a preliminary injunction may be based on a fact which arose after the injunction was granted (e.g., complainant assigned all his interest in the future duration of the patent; omitted to prosecute with required speed; advertised the injunction falsely; prior adjudication reversed on appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: assignment of future interest, failure to prosecute, false advertising, reversal on appeal. These subsequent facts can justify dissolving a preliminary injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to dissolve for error in point of law — limited grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to dissolve an injunction for error in point of law must be based on a point established after the injunction was granted, or one obviously overlooked or misweighed by the judge at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should not move to dissolve merely because the judge wrongly reasoned from premises; courts should not be asked to change judgments on points of law unless the law has changed or some special error is pointed out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on mover for newly discovered facts
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to dissolve an injunction on account of newly discovered facts requires the mover to assume the burden of establishing those facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because an injunction once granted is presumed rightly granted until the contrary is shown, affidavits and other evidence may be introduced by both parties; the judge must weigh the papers and decide against the mover unless mover's papers preponderate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of affidavits before motion hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Service on the opposite party, before the motion is heard, of the affidavits upon which a motion to dissolve an injunction is made or resisted is called for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning parallels service requirements for affidavits in support/opposition of preliminary injunction motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of dissolved injunction — changed circumstances required
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to reinstate a dissolved injunction may be made at any time, but will not be granted on the same state of the case as that which existed when the injunction was dissolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reinstated preliminary injunction may again be dissolved on any new state of facts showing continuation would be unjust. Courts will rarely alternate issuing and dissolving preliminary injunctions in patent cases absent clearness and pressing necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience to injunction while in force
rubrics_metrics.description: While an injunction is in force, it must be obeyed, even though it ought never to have been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: an injunction is not in force if issued against a person over whom the court had no jurisdiction; orders without authority are nullities. If jurisdiction is later obtained by timely service, the injunction must be obeyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons bound by injunction beyond named defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction is binding upon all persons who were connected with the defendant in defending against the suit before issuance and who were connected in disobeying after being informed of its issue, even if they were not themselves defendants nor served with the writ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a mere order for an injunction, upon which no writ is ever issued, is not binding on anybody; a served writ can retroact to cover disobedient acts occurring after notice and before formal issuance/serving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of bond or damages order as condition for injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: When an injunction is granted, courts may order the complainant to pay resulting damages if injunction later proves wrongful, or require the complainant to file a bond to secure those damages as a condition precedent to issuing the injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent such order or bond, the enjoined party may be without redress if injunction ought not to have been granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal interlocutory injunction orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is demandable to the Circuit Court of Appeals from any District Court order which grants, continues, refuses or dissolves an interlocutory order or decree, or refuses to dissolve an injunction, within thirty days from entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'hearing in equity' for purposes of the statute means presentation/submission of the motion; such appeals take precedence in the appellate court but do not stay other proceedings below unless ordered. Appeal does not automatically give right to supersedeas; suspension pending appeal is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate review standard for preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellate court will not reverse an order granting a preliminary injunction unless it clearly appears the court below exercised its discretion upon a wholly wrong comprehension of the facts or law; but will not follow plainly wrong or insufficient decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on providence of injunction may depend, according to circumstances, on ultimate merits; adjudication relied upon below generally has similar strength on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent expiration on appeals and injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal from a preliminary injunction will be dismissed without adjudication when the patent has expired since the injunction was granted because the injunction will have terminated at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where order required defendant to give bond or be enjoined and defendant gave bond, the order will not usually be reviewed on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent injunction following interlocutory victory
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent injunction follows a decision in favor of the complainant on the interlocutory hearing of a patent case unless some special reason exists for refusal, postponement until after master's report, or suspension pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule: victory on interlocutory merits leads to permanent injunction absent special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of permanent injunction when patent expired
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal of a permanent injunction will generally follow from the fact that the patent has expired at the time of the interlocutory decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible exception limited to preventing use/sale after expiration of specimens made before expiration — courts generally avoid prolonging patent term by injunction; damages are adequate remedy. No injunction to prevent preparing during patent life for post-expiration use/sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal when complainant assigned future interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal of a permanent injunction will be necessary where the complainant is shown to have assigned, prior to the interlocutory decree, all his interest in the future duration of the patent right infringed by the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment of future interest defeats need for injunction directed to future relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-use of invention and injunction jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of equity to grant an injunction is not affected by length of non-use or by the motive of the owner in withholding it from use (Continental Paper Bag decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior doubts resolved: mere non-working does not preclude injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of permanent injunction for defendant hardship
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent injunction will be postponed until a final decree when such postponement is necessary to save the defendant from special hardship and is not injurious to the complainant's just rights, or when immediate discontinuance is contrary to public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent has short time to run, security for recovery of damages and profits may be permitted in lieu of injunction; when postponement allowed, defendant should give bond for complainant's security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of injunction pending appeal — bond security
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent injunction may be suspended pending an appeal at the discretion of the judge who decided the case, upon such terms as to bond or otherwise as proper to secure the opposite party's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond should be conditioned upon appeal result and secure profits and damages to accrue after interlocutory decree and before appellate decision, and possibly those accruing thereafter pending Supreme Court review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension pending final-decree appeal — extraordinary cause
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent injunction may be suspended, for an extraordinary cause, pending an appeal from a final decree to the Circuit Court of Appeals, at judge's discretion, upon terms securing complainant's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security must include profits and damages accruing after final decree in addition to supersedeas bond for earlier accruals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolution of permanent injunction post-judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent injunction may be dissolved at any time within six months after the expiration of the term of court at which the final decree was entered, where defendant secures cancellation by supplemental bill or bill of review, and must be dissolved whenever the decree is reversed by a higher court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural vehicle: bill of review/supplemental bill; reversal mandates dissolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions may be granted independent of other relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Injunctions to restrain infringements of patents may be granted independent of all other relief; an injunction may restrain a complainant from bringing an action at law against the defendant for the same infringements as those covered by the equity action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But no injunction will be issued for trivial infringements below the court's dignity, nor to restrain a junior patentee from bringing actions while patent is free from adjudication of invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of enjoining suits against users/dealers — conflicting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it is proper to enjoin a complainant from bringing actions against users or sellers of articles is conflicting; when action is against a manufacturer and bill asks for accounting of all damages and profits, a suit against a user or dealer will be enjoined if recovery would release articles from the patent monopoly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicting authority — application depends on facts, relief sought, and circuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kessler v. Eldred doctrine on protecting manufacturer's business
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacturer defendant who has prevailed on infringement in a Circuit Court of Appeals is entitled to an injunction protecting his right to continue manufacturing and selling the same item without molestation by the patentee, and to bar plaintiff from suing the manufacturer's customers in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine protects successful defendant's business from wrongful interference by patentee; scope limited (does not necessarily bar suits against purchasers who assemble components).

rubrics_metrics.name: No injunction against truthful notices to customers
rubrics_metrics.description: No injunction will issue to restrain a plaintiff from sending circulars to defendant's customers giving notice of the suit and warning against contributory infringement where statements are true and sent in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misleading or exaggerated notices calculated to injury defendant's legitimate business may be grounds to dissolve injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction to stay infringement suit pending patent issuance action
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction will issue on application of a plaintiff in a suit to compel issuance of a patent under Section 4915 of the Revised Statutes, to stay a suit brought by the defendant to enjoin infringement of the patent, until the Section 4915 suit is decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable stay protects the Section 4915 proceeding's outcome; procedural posture matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of injunctions limited by patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless expressly made to apply to use or sale after patent expiration of specimens made before that time, an injunction cannot continue after patent expiration; no injunction ought to continue after expiration of the patent as patent rights are not perpetual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injunctions also should not be made to apply to unpatented parts of an infringing combination; injunctive relief is bounded by the life of the underlying right.

rubrics_metrics.name: In personam power limited by territorial scope of patent monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: The court having jurisdiction over defendants may control them by decree in personam from doing any act within or without the jurisdiction that interferes with plaintiff's rights; but because a patent monopoly extends only to United States territory, courts cannot enjoin the bringing of a suit on a foreign patent for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable decrees operate in personam against persons subject to the court's jurisdiction; they cannot create extraterritorial patent monopolies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement by attachment for contempt — service and description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An attachment will issue to bring an enjoined defendant before the court for punishment when complainant proves defendant was promptly served with the writ of injunction and that the writ contained a concise description of the particular thing (all specimens) which it forbade the defendant to make, use, or sell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of prompt service and sufficient specificity in the writ are prerequisites to contempt proceedings.
